name: Champion of Martial Fury
body:
Champions of Martial Fury dedicate themselves to the relentless pursuit of victory in battle. They draw strength from the ferocity and martial prowess of Ares, channeling it into their combat skills and their unwavering determination. These fierce warriors embody the spirit of unyielding courage and disciplined aggression.

Background: Most Champions of Martial Fury began their careers as warriors serving and protecting their community. Many come from humble, rural upbringings and are members of a warrior society.

Ancestries: Ares’ followers are usually human, though giant kin, dwarves, and others are also found among their ranks.

Homeland: Most Champions of Martial Fury are from southern Italia, Anatolia, Greece, Italia, and Scythia. A few are from Gaul or North Africa. Rarely are Ares’ followers found in lands further away such as Persia or Iberia.

Role: Champions of Martial Fury are ferocious warriors who prefer to be on the front lines of combat. They eagerly seek out battle and will use any pretense to fight. Because of these traits, these warriors function best as heavy infantry and assault troops.

Religion: Champions of Ares are always devoted to Ares and his doctrine of brutal, chaotic war. This doesn’t preclude these champions from honoring or worshiping other deities, but it does mean they hold Ares above all others.

Alignment: Champions of Martial Fury embrace chaos, making it part of their being. Ares emphasizes the horrific, confusing, and brutal aspects of war. For these reasons Champions of Martial Fury must be some form of Chaotic alignment.

Adventures: Champions of Martial Fury lead lives of harrowing adventure. Constantly moving from one war to another, they live in barracks, training yards, and battlefields. They work as soldiers or mercenaries, be it infantry, reconnaissance, or cavalry. As cult members, they might also be assigned tasks related to the temple. They may be required to travel to Metropolis or another distant city where Ares has a major temple. Or they might be sent to any of the smaller shrines and temples to deliver messages, undergo special training, or assist in a military operation. Rarely, they may be called upon to secure a powerful magic item, such as the Sword of Ares.

Promises

The following are the sacred promises made by a Champion of Martial Fury:

Mighty Wrath: Harness your anger and unleash it upon your enemies. Righteous fury is a powerful force that drives you to overcome all obstacles on the battlefield.
Unrelenting Discipline: Adhere to strict training and unwavering discipline to hone your martial skills. Through rigorous physical and mental conditioning, you will become a perfect instrument of war.
Conquest and Glory: Establish a lasting legacy of conquest and earn glory in the annals of history as a champion of Ares.
Battlefield Supremacy: Master the art of warfare in all its forms. Whether it be skill with weapons, tactics, or commanding troops, strive to be a beacon of inspiration on the battlefield, leading your allies to victory and striking fear into the hearts of your enemies.

Hit Die: d10.

Requirements

To qualify to become a Champion of Martial Fury, a character must fulfill all the following criteria.

Base Attack Bonus: +3.
Skills: Intimidation 3 ranks, Knowledge (war) 3 ranks.
Alignment: Any chaotic.
Class Skills

The Champion of Martial Fury’s class skills are Craft (Int), Handle Animal (Cha), Heal (Wis), Intimidate (Cha), Knowledge (religion) (Int), Knowledge (war) (Int), Profession (Wis), Ride (Dex), Sense Motive (Wis), and Spellcraft (Int).

Skill Ranks per Level: 2 + Int modifier.

Class Features

All of the following are class features of the Champion of Martial Fury.

Chosen Enemy (Su)

At 1st level, as a swift action, a Martial Fury can select one creature within sight to be their chosen enemy. The target remains the chosen enemy until it is killed or 24 hours have elapsed, whichever comes first. The Martial Fury adds their Charisma modifier (if positive) to their attack rolls and adds double their Martial Fury level to all damage rolls made against the chosen enemy. Additionally, the Martial Fury gains a deflection bonus to their AC equal to their Martial Fury level (maximum 5) against their chosen enemy. At 4th level and every three levels thereafter, the Martial Fury may designate a chosen enemy one additional time per day, as indicated on Table 1: Champion of Martial Fury.

War Cry (Su)

At 1st level, as a swift action, a Martial Fury can unleash a powerful war cry that motivates allies and frightens enemies. For the next minute, the Martial Fury and all friendly creatures within 30 feet gain a morale bonus on saving throw rolls equal to the Martial Fury’s Charisma modifier (minimum of 1). Any hostile creatures within the same range must make a successful Will saving throw or become frightened for 1 minute. A Martial Fury can use this ability a number of times per day equal to her Charisma modifier (minimum of 1).

Spells. Beginning at 1st level, a champion gains the ability to cast a small number of divine spells which are drawn from the paladin spell list. A champion must choose and prepare her spells in advance.

To prepare or cast a spell, a champion must have a Charisma score equal to at least 10 + the spell level. The Difficulty Class for a saving throw against a champion’s spell is 10 + the spell level + the champion’s Charisma modifier.

Like other spellcasters, a champion can cast only a certain number of spells of each spell level per day.

Her base daily spell allotment is given on Table 1: Champion of Martial Fury. In addition, she receives bonus spells per day if she has a high Charisma score (see Table: Ability Modifiers and Bonus Spells).

When Table 1 indicates that the champion gets 0 spells per day of a given spell level, she gains only the bonus spells she would be entitled to based on her Charisma score for that spell level.

A champion must spend 1 hour each day in quiet prayer and meditation to regain her daily allotment of spells. A champion may prepare and cast any spell on the paladin spell list, provided that she can cast spells of that level, but she must choose which spells to prepare during her daily meditation.

Wrathful Strike (Ex)

Once per day as a free action, the Martial Fury can make a special melee attack that bypasses all damage reduction and spell resistance of the target. Whether the attack hits or not, this ability is still expended.

Regimented Training (Ex)

The training of a Martial Fury is unparalleled. Martial Furies are conditioned to withstand assaults to their bodies and minds, and to react quickly and decisively against such attacks. At 2nd level, a Martial Fury gains a +1 circumstance bonus on all saving throws.

They also gain immunity to charm spells and spell-like abilities.

Aura of Courage (Su)

At 3rd level, a Champion of Martial Fury is immune to fear (magical or otherwise). Each ally within 10 feet of her gains a +4 morale bonus on saving throws against fear effects.

This ability functions only while the champion is conscious, not if she is unconscious or dead.

Divine Health (Ex)

At 3rd level, a Champion of Martial Fury is immune to all diseases, including supernatural and magical diseases, including mummy rot.

Martial Training (Ex)

At 3rd level and again at 9th level, a Champion of Martial Fury can select one group of weapons from the fighter’s weapon groups.

Whenever a Martial Fury attacks with a weapon from the chosen group, she gains a +2 bonus on attack and damage rolls. The Martial Fury also adds this bonus to any Combat Maneuver checks made with weapons from the selected group. This bonus also applies to the Martial Fury’s CMD when defending against disarm and sunder attempts made against weapons from the selected group.

Furthermore, if the weapon group selected contains exotic weapons, the Martial Fury is treated as though she has the Exotic Weapon Proficiency feat for those weapons.

This setting has a few unique weapons not found in the Pathfinder fighter weapon groups. Refer to the information below to determine which fighter weapon groups these weapons belong to.

Bolster Chaos (Su)

When a Champion of Martial Fury reaches 4th level, she gains the supernatural ability to channel a burst of chaotic energy. All chaotic creatures in a 30-foot radius of the Martial Fury gain a +2 circumstance bonus to their attack rolls while lawfully aligned creatures in the area must make a Will save (DC 10 + the Martial Fury’s class level + her Cha modifier) or suffer a -2 penalty to attack rolls. The Martial Fury may use this ability a number of times per day equal to her Charisma modifier (minimum 1).

Divine Bond (Sp)

At 5th level, a champion forms a divine bond with her god. This bond can take one of two forms. Once the form is chosen, it cannot be changed.

Bonded Weapon. The first type of bond allows the champion to enhance her weapon as a standard action by calling upon the aid of a daemonic spirit for 1 minute per champion level. When called, the spirit causes the weapon to shed light as a torch. At 1st level, this spirit grants the weapon a +1 enhancement bonus. For every three levels beyond 1st, the weapon gains another +1 enhancement bonus. These bonuses can be added to the weapon, stacking with existing weapon bonuses to a maximum of +5, or they can be used to add any of the following weapon properties: anarchic, brilliant energy, defending, disruption, flaming, flaming burst, keen, speed and stalking. Adding these properties consumes an amount of bonus equal to the property’s cost (see Table: Magic Weapon Special Abilities). These bonuses are added to any properties the weapon already has, but duplicate abilities do not stack. If the weapon is not magical, at least a +1 enhancement bonus must be added before any other properties can be added. The bonus and properties granted by the spirit are determined when the spirit is called and cannot be changed until the spirit is called again. The daemonic spirit imparts no bonuses if the weapon is held by anyone other than the champion but resumes giving bonuses if returned to the champion. These bonuses apply to only one end of a double weapon. A champion can use this ability once per day at 5th level, and one additional time per day for every four levels beyond 5th.

If a weapon bonded with a daemonic spirit is destroyed, the champion loses the use of this ability for 30 days, or until she gains a level, whichever comes first. During this 30-day period, the champion takes a –1 penalty on attack and weapon damage rolls.

Bonded Mount. The second type of bond allows a champion to gain the service of an unusually intelligent, strong, and loyal steed to serve her in her crusades. This creature is usually a heavy horse (for a Medium champion) or a pony (for a Small champion), although more exotic mounts, such as a boar, camel, or dog are also suitable. This mount functions as a druid’s animal companion, using the champion’s total character level as her effective druid level. Bonded mounts have an Intelligence of at least 6.

In addition to horses, a champion may select (at the GM’s discretion) some less ordinary creatures.

A Medium champion can select an elk, giant seahorse, giraffe, yak or zebra as a bonded mount.

A Small champion can select an antelope, capybara, eohippus, giant weasel, ram, reindeer, stag, or wolfdog as a bonded mount.

Upon reaching 6th level as a champion or 16th level in total character levels, whichever comes first, the champion can choose a flying horse, giant eagle, Pegasus, griffon, giant hawk, giant vulture, or giant owl as a bonded mount.

The auspice, bodyguard, racer, and totem guide archetypes are all particularly appropriate for a champion’s bonded mount.

Once per day, as a full-round action, a champion may magically call her mount to her side. This ability is the equivalent of a spell of a level equal to one third the champion’s level. The mount immediately appears adjacent to the champion. A champion can use this ability once per day at 5th level, and one additional time per day at 9th level.

Should the champion’s mount die, the champion may not summon another mount for 30 days or until she gains a champion or War Spawn level, whichever comes first. During this 30-day period, the champion takes a –1 penalty on attack and weapon damage rolls.

Regimented Training II (Ex)

By 6th level, a Champion of Martial Fury gains immunity to compulsion spells and spell-like abilities.

Chaotic Combatant

At 7th level, Champions of Martial Fury add the rage spell to their spell list.

Bonus Feat (Ex)

At 8th level, a Champion of Martial Fury gains a bonus feat in addition to those gained from normal advancement. This bonus feat must be selected from those listed as Combat Feats.

Greater Chosen Enemy (Su)

At 10th level, the damage from the champion’s chosen enemy ability increases to 3 extra points per champion level.
